guideSummary.surfnerd: Baishawan is a north-facing, white sand beach break with easy access from Taipei on the train and bus. It is often flat through summer, and in winter it turns cold and windy with little power or shape, which is why it tends to draw kiteboarders, windsurfers and hang gliders as much as surfers. If you want a better wave nearby, the high-tide reefbreak called Wedding Plaza sits a little further east, and closer to town at Danshuei, Shalun Beach can throw up a messy, rolling wave for beginners.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Paishawan Beach in - is a reasonably exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the east southeast. Windswells are much more common than groundswells and the ideal wave angle is from the northeast. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. Rarely crowded here. Watch out for rocks.
